kept.heading: HOW GEN Z KILLED MILLENNIAL MINIMALISM (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Packaging is splitting from the clean, muted, Instagram-minimal look that defined brands like Glossier and Warby Parker toward louder colors, illustration, and visible imperfection. The shift shows up across categories that once signaled seriousness through restraint: soda alternatives adopting soda-bright packaging, wellness brands trading polish for handmade textures, and hand sanitizer redesigned as a beauty accessory worth carrying. The change isn't really about killing minimalism - it's about killing sameness, since the muted aesthetic stopped differentiating once every brand copied it.

Title: How Gen Z Killed Millennial Minimalism

URL Source: https://thebrandblueprint.substack.com/p/how-gen-z-killed-millennial-minimalism

Published Time: 2026-08-26T14:18:51+00:00

Markdown Content:
[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!zbc4!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3162d06c-256f-4541-a329-885ca13d83ea_1920x1080.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!zbc4!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3162d06c-256f-4541-a329-885ca13d83ea_1920x1080.png)

Happy Wednesday!

Today I want to talk about packaging because we are in the middle of a pretty massive shift in what makes a brand look “cool”.

For years, the formula was simple. Make the packaging minimal, use a clean sans serif font, pick a muted color palette, and make sure everything looked perfect on Instagram.

And it worked. Some of the biggest millennial brands were built around that exact aesthetic.

But now walk through Sephora, Erewhon, Target, or scroll through TikTok and everything looks different. The packaging is brighter, fonts are weirderr, and every brand has crazy illustrations everywhere. Brands are less afraid of looking a little chaotic.

Gen Z is screaming life into brands again.

And I don’t think this is just another design trend. Packaging reflects the customer you’re trying to reach, and Gen Z has a very different idea of what makes a brand feel interesting.

So let’s talk about how Gen Z killed millennial minimalism.

P.S. The founder of Everlane is building the next $1B supplement brand called **[Magna](https://www.drinkmagna.com/BLUEPRINT10)**. Magnesium powered hydration to fuel focus, energy, and recovery. I started talking it a few weeks ago and I’m obsessed. Here’s my magna discount code **[link](https://www.drinkmagna.com/BLUEPRINT10)** to get 29% off the starter kit.

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!yTyI!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4a54d3f9-3169-4bd2-bca9-f7b3b9412afc_1920x1080.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!yTyI!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4a54d3f9-3169-4bd2-bca9-f7b3b9412afc_1920x1080.png)

Before we talk about where packaging is going, we have to talk about what came before it.

Millennial packaging was minimalist, clean, aspirational, and extremely Instagram friendly.

Think [Glossier](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077523), [Away](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077583), [Warby Parker](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077548), or [Outdoor Voices](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077596).

The aesthetic was easy to recognize. Clean fonts, muted colors, lots of negative space, simple logos, centered layouts, and perfectly art directed photography.

At the time, it felt completely different from the loud, overly branded products millennials had grown up with. Stripping everything back made brands feel modern, elevated, and premium.

It also happened alongside the rise of Instagram, when products needed to look good in carefully curated feeds. And it worked incredibly well. Almost every brand wanted to copy the Glossier playbook at the time.

But once every new brand adopted the same visual language, what once felt different started making every brand look the same.

Gen Z grew up surrounded by millennial minimalism, so naturally, the next generation of brands is rebelling against it.

Now Gen Z packaging can be colorful, weird, nostalgic, handmade, feminine, chaotic, or incredibly simple. What connects the brands doing it well is that they actually feel like they have a point of view.

So here are the shifts I am noticing and my favorite examples.

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!M3Lc!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F1ff545e5-c188-4c45-ba38-bfeb52f3dbae_1442x616.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!M3Lc!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F1ff545e5-c188-4c45-ba38-bfeb52f3dbae_1442x616.png)

For a long time, better for you products almost had to _look_ healthy.

Muted colors, minimal labels, lots of white space, and branding that immediately told you this was the responsible option.

But why does have to look boring?

**[OLIPOP](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077630)** is a great example of how that’s changing.

The brand made its packaging brighter and bolder, enlarged the flavor illustrations, and moved toward playful lowercase typography that gives each flavor more personality.

**Why it works**

If your packaging constantly reminds customers they’re choosing the “healthy alternative,” you’re reinforcing the idea that they’re making a compromise.

OLIPOP visually competes with soda by actually looking fun.

**Thoughts to ask for your brand**

*   Does your packaging communicate the benefit so heavily that you’ve forgotten to make the product desirable?

*   Could your category afford to take itself a little less seriously?

[![Image 4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!mXGU!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6d4b4b9d-cb41-40fe-8cfa-e2fcab251de8_1436x552.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!mXGU!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6d4b4b9d-cb41-40fe-8cfa-e2fcab251de8_1436x552.png)

This is probably one of the clearest differences between millennial and Gen Z branding.

Millennial packaging often tried to remove anything unnecessary. Gen Z packaging is much more comfortable adding it back.

**[Fishwife](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077648)** is one of my favorite examples.

Canned fish historically wasn’t exactly a category known for packaging people wanted to display. Fishwife completely changed that.

Its tins are colorful, illustrative, maximalist, and filled with personality. They almost feel more like little pieces of art than something you’d find in the canned seafood aisle.

**Why it works**

Fishwife didn’t need to reinvent canned fish. It needed to make canned fish feel relevant to a new customer.

The packaging makes an ordinary grocery product interesting enough to display, photograph, gift, and talk about.

**Thoughts to ask for your brand**

*   If someone covered your logo, would your packaging still feel recognizable?

*   What could your packaging communicate about the personality of the person buying it?

[![Image 5](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!l56W!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Ffe518ac0-b3c8-4ede-a7a8-d3cb01e90fb5_1416x582.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!l56W!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Ffe518ac0-b3c8-4ede-a7a8-d3cb01e90fb5_1416x582.png)

Brands used to spend a lot of money making sure everything looked perfectly polished.

Gen Z seems much more comfortable with things that feel handmade, slightly weird, or intentionally imperfect.

**[Coconut Cult](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077766)** does this really well.

The glass jars, chunky typography, bright colors, and hand drawn illustrations make the product feel like something you discovered at a local market instead of a highly polished wellness brand.

**Why it works**

When an entire category starts using the same polished design language, imperfection becomes differentiation.

Coconut Cult’s packaging feels human and slightly weird, which makes the brand harder to confuse with everything else on shelf.

**Thoughts to ask for your brand**

*   Is your brand so polished that you’ve removed some of its personality?

*   What could feel more handmade, unexpected, or human?

[![Image 6](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!hxoN!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb601bbe5-3b47-40a7-813b-0668e7d117c1_1840x792.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!hxoN!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb601bbe5-3b47-40a7-813b-0668e7d117c1_1840x792.png)

Packaging is not just competing for attention on a retail shelf anymore. It is also competing for a permanent spot on someone’s counter.

**[Graza](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077795)** is a perfect example of this.

Traditional olive oil bottles were designed to live in the pantry. Graza turned olive oil into a bright green squeeze bottle that feels more like a design object than a kitchen staple.

**Why it works**

When a product earns a permanent place on someone’s counter, the packaging keeps marketing the brand long after the purchase.

**Thoughts to ask for your brand**

*   Would your customer want to leave your product out after they use it?

*   Could your packaging become part of their space instead of something they hide away?

[![Image 7](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!qe-A!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4b57b234-fc35-4f0e-acf6-2c99c32417e2_1790x812.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!qe-A!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4b57b234-fc35-4f0e-acf6-2c99c32417e2_1790x812.png)

Another shift I find really interesting is how Gen Z brands approach categories traditionally built around insecurity. We’re seeing this happen in skincare, specifically acne products.

Traditional acne products tend to look clinical because the category is built around the idea that acne is a problem you need to fix and hide.

**[Starface](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077823)** went in the complete opposite direction.

Bright yellow packaging, bubbly typography, colorful collectible cases, and little stars customers intentionally put on their faces.

**Why it works**

Starface changed the emotional experience of the category.

Instead of making customers feel like they need to hide the fact that they’re treating a breakout, the brand makes the experience playful enough to show off.

**Thoughts to ask for your brand**

*   What emotion has your category traditionally made customers feel?

*   Could your packaging completely change that emotion?

[![Image 8](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!wAXS!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6b45c2e6-9b82-4329-968c-13ffd16778fd_2198x874.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!wAXS!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6b45c2e6-9b82-4329-968c-13ffd16778fd_2198x874.png)

Some of the biggest packaging opportunities are hiding in the most boring categories.

When nobody expects a product to look good, good design can completely change its perceived value.

**[Touchland](https://go.shopmy.us/p-81077922)** changed this for hand sanitizer.

Before Touchland, most hand sanitizer came in a basic plastic bottle that you threw into your bag and forgot about.

Touchland redesigned it as a slim, flat, colorful spray that feels much closer to a beauty accessory.

**Why it works**

Touchland didn’t just redesign hand sanitizer packaging. It changed the role the product could play in someone’s life. They turned a commodity became an accessory.

**Thoughts to ask for your brand**

*   What does everyone in your category accept as boring because “that’s how it’s always looked”?

*   Could better packaging turn your functional product into something customers actually want to carry?

I don’t think Gen Z killed minimalism. I think they killed sameness.

Millennial minimalism worked because it once felt different. Then every brand started looking the same.

Gen Z brands are breaking those rules in completely different ways, but once that aesthetic starts feeling overdone too, we may see the pendulum swing back again.

There isn’t one Gen Z aesthetic to copy. The shift is from packaging designed to look perfect to packaging designed to have a personality.

Now definitely respond to this with your thoughts on all of this.

Have a great rest of your week!

-Brooke

kept.heading: HOW MUCH OF THE INTERNET IS WRITTEN WITH AI? (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: About 10% of webpages now show significant signs of AI authorship, rising to more than one-third of pages published since ChatGPT launched. AI-written content is also becoming easier to spot, with phrases, vocabulary, and punctuation associated with AI appearing more often across the web. The trend is strongest on .com sites, where AI authorship appears roughly 2X as often as on .org and 10X more than on .edu and .gov sites.

Title: How Much of the Internet Is Written With AI?

URL Source: https://www.pewresearch.org/data-labs/2026/08/20/how-much-of-the-internet-is-written-with-ai/

Published Time: 2026-08-20T11:55:49-04:00

Markdown Content:
![Image 1](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/08/pl_2026.08.20_ai-content_dots.png?w=140&h=140&crop=1)

August 20, 2026

In November 2022, OpenAI released ChatGPT to the public for the first time. Less than four years later, around half of U.S. adults say they [use chatbots](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2026/06/17/americans-and-ai-2026-chatbots-smart-devices-and-views-on-impact/) powered by artificial intelligence, including 24% who say they use them daily. These tools’ ability to generate human-sounding text has raised a basic question about the modern web: How much content online is now written by AI rather than by other people?

To explore this question, we used the [Common Crawl](https://commoncrawl.org/) web archive to collect almost half a million English-language webpages from the past five years – starting a couple of years before the release of ChatGPT. We then ran the text of those pages through an AI detection tool called [Open Pangram](https://www.pangram.com/blog/introducing-open-pangram) to see how many of them were likely written or substantially edited by AI.

AI-authored text is not evenly spread across the web. When ChatGPT was first released, the kinds of linguistic patterns that can signal AI authorship appeared at similar rates across the main top-level web domains (.com, .org, .edu and .gov).

But in samples from 2026, **around one-in-ten pages with a .com domain** show signs of AI authorship – about double the share on .org domains (4.6%), and 10 times the rate on .edu or .gov domains (both around 1%).

Note: Plotted points represent six-month averages.

Source: Pew Research Center analysis of 490,000 English-language webpage texts sampled from the Common Crawl web repository and analyzed using Open Pangram.

PEW RESEARCH CENTER

* * *

### What are some common features of AI-authored text?

AI detection models aren’t perfect – they sometimes misclassify individual documents that were written by humans as including signs of AI authorship, and vice versa. But if we look at very large collections of texts together, we can start to see that certain types of **punctuation, words and phrases** show up at much higher rates in AI-generated content than in text written by humans.

WRITTEN BY AI

The internet has evolved into something far beyond a simple network of connected pages — it’s a living, shifting ecosystem shaped by algorithms, creators, and audiences alike, bolstered by waves of AI-generated content that blur the lines between human and machine expression.As users keep delving in to endless streams of posts, videos, and synthetic voices, a pivotal question emerges about authenticity, ownership, and trust—because it’s not just information, it’s influence.

1.   Em dashes
2.   Oxford commas
3.   AI vocabulary
4.    Negative parallelism

AI models are trained on large datasets of human writing, and they learn to mimic the patterns and styles of that writing. Sometimes certain types of writing are overrepresented in that training process. As a result, models trained on that data can end up using certain words, phrases or linguistic quirks [more than humans typically do](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/03/magazine/chatbot-writing-style.html).

For instance, lots of journalistic and academic writing uses the em dash (—), which is a punctuation mark used to indicate a break in thought or set off a parenthetical statement. AI models tend to use these dashes a lot more than humans typically do. They’re also more likely than human authors to list items in threes and to use Oxford commas in lists.

And as more AI-generated content appears online, these and other AI “tells” have become more common across webpages. Comparing the internet of today to a snapshot from 2023:

*   Em dashes appear about twice as frequently.
*   Oxford commas see a 63% increase.
*   Certain words that AI models like to use (such as “delve,” “interplay” or “testament”) have more than doubled in usage.
*   Using “negative parallelism” to structure a comparison (“it’s not just X, it’s Y”) has nearly tripled – although this is still fairly rare overall.

Of course, em dashes or Oxford commas on their own don’t necessarily mean a particular piece of writing was produced using AI – humans use these in their writing too! But if we look at _a lot_ of documents together, we can start to see patterns in how often human authors and AI models reach for these features on average. And sophisticated detection models like the one we used for this analysis have more to go on than just looking for a few telltale signals. They also learn to recognize more subtle statistical patterns in word choice and sentence structure which help them determine whether a particular piece of writing was likely AI-authored.

About this research
This Pew Research Center essay explores how signs of AI-authored text have increased across the internet over the years since mainstream AI-powered chatbots first hit the market.

**Why did we do this?**

Pew Research Center does research to help the public, media and decision-makers understand important topics. Tracking the [rise of AI](https://www.pewresearch.org/topic/internet-technology/emerging-technology/artificial-intelligence/) and understanding people’s experiences with it are key priorities for us.

Learn more about [Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/about/) and our [data science research](https://www.pewresearch.org/data-labs/).

**How did we do this?**

The data for this essay comes from [Common Crawl](https://commoncrawl.org/latest-crawl) web archive snapshots collected between January 2021 and July 2026. To analyze this data, we used an open-weight AI detection model created by [Pangram](https://www.pangram.com/blog/introducing-open-pangram). Models like this one look for statistical differences in how human authors and AI models use language, helping them identify when a text shows signs of AI authorship.

Read more about how we did this in this essay’s [methodology](https://www.pewresearch.org/data-labs/2026/08/20/methodology-ai-content/).

# How TextNow learned when YouTube awareness starts driving lower-funnel lift

26 weeks of YouTube treatment

1.84%total W2PU lift after the post-treatment window

87%of the measured effect accumulated after the first two months

Seeing results like this gives us confidence that this kind of media can work for us. It also helps us understand when to expect the impact, because the time horizon is very different.

![Image 4: Bonnie Herche](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/63c00db03ecb8a822c829783/6a8c6b680b6fbd2c77cb678c_Bonnie%20Herche%20textnow.png)

Bonnie Herche

Vice President of Marketing, TextNow

Company

TextNow

[Visit](https://www.textnow.com/)

Industry

YouTube

Features used

GeoLift

## The challenge

### Measure brand with rigor, but not on a performance-media clock

TextNow makes it possible for people to stay connected through free and flexible phone service. Its growth team had built a mature incrementality program to understand which media investments were generating outcomes that would not have happened otherwise.

The team’s next question was harder. TextNow was preparing to invest further up the funnel and wanted to know whether YouTube campaigns optimized for reach and video completion could eventually influence lower-funnel behavior.

Platform studies could show whether the campaign affected brand metrics. They could not show how many users became active because of the campaign. TextNow wanted to measure that impact against Total Week 2 Primary Users, or Total W2PU, a business KPI that captures users who remain active into their second week.

But awareness media might not produce an immediate lower-funnel response, making a short test easy to misread. TextNow did not just need to know whether YouTube worked. It needed to understand when YouTube’s impact would become visible in the outcome the business cared about.

> We need to measure our brand like we measure our performance, but brand doesn’t act like performance.

Bonnie Herche, Vice President of Marketing, TextNow

## The solution

TextNow partnered with Haus to run a 26-week geo experiment from December 2025 through May 2026, followed by a six-week post-treatment window.

The team geo-fenced 20% of the United States, drawn as an 80/20 design so the smaller partition behaved like a scaled-down version of the country rather than a convenient set of markets. Half of those markets received YouTube reach and video-completion media, while the other half formed a holdout for estimating incremental Total W2PUs. Business-as-usual media was designed to stay balanced across both groups, and TextNow could keep running other experiments across the rest of the country.

The design let TextNow track whether lower-funnel lift emerged, when it became visible, and how the measured result changed after media stopped.

| Test | **YouTube Awareness** Reach + Video Completion |
| --- |
| Test Type | 2-cell with holdout |
| Region | 20% US geo-fence Representative 80/20 draw 50% exposed / 50% holdout |
| Time | 26 weeks + 6-week post-treatment window |
| Primary KPI | Total Week 2 Primary Users |

### Readout schedule

| Dec | Treatment begins |
| --- |
| Jan | Month-one readout |
| Mar | Midpoint readout |
| May | Treatment ends |
| Jul | Post-treatment readout |

> We wanted to understand the payback period for upper-funnel media: what we saw in brand lift, what we saw in search lift, what we saw in KPI lift, and when each effect showed up.

Nick Hughes, Growth Marketing Lead, TextNow

## The result

### The first month missed the story

For roughly the first five weeks, cumulative lift hovered around zero.

Had TextNow ended the experiment after four to six weeks, the early read could have understated or missed the lower-funnel effect that emerged later. Instead, TextNow kept the experiment running.

The pattern began to change in late January. Two months into the test, cumulative incremental Total W2PUs stood at roughly 13% of their eventual level, which means about 87% of the measured effect accumulated after the first two months. By early March the cumulative result had reached about half its final level, with the clearest gains emerging through February.

The path was not perfectly linear. But the cumulative view told a clear practical story: The first month did not capture the effect visible in the complete read.

![Image 5](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/63c00db03ecb8a822c829783/6a8c7cbc985280619ed593e3_figure1_indexed_lift%402x.png)

**Figure 1.**Cumulative incremental Total Week 2 Primary Users stayed near zero early, then built across the six-month treatment and remained positive through the observation window. Values are indexed so the final read equals 100.

### Efficiency became meaningful only after lift had time to build

At the end of the 26-week treatment period, the experiment measured a 1.99% lift in Total W2PU at an indexed cost per incremental user (CPIA) of 106, or roughly 6% above the experiment’s planning assumption.

Including the six-week post-treatment window raised the point estimate and lowered measured cost per incremental user by roughly 8%, bringing the result just inside the planning assumption:

*   **1.84%**Total W2PU lift
*   **98**indexed CPIA, against a planning assumption of 100, so roughly 2% inside plan
*   **~8%**improvement in measured efficiency versus the treatment-only read

![Image 6](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/63c00db03ecb8a822c829783/6a8c7ca9f8fe57a27dd01f84_figure2_indexed_cpia%402x.png)

**Figure 2.**The early efficiency read was unstable because lift had not emerged yet. Once the cumulative result developed, running CPIA moved toward the experiment’s planning assumption. Values are indexed so the planning assumption equals 100.

### One test gave TextNow a way to compare awareness and direct response

Until this test, TextNow had limited evidence for judging awareness media on lower-funnel outcomes. YouTube changed that.

It finished at an index of 98, slightly better than plan. It did not beat TextNow’s median test at 62, but it came in below several scaled prospecting programs despite being optimized for reach and video completion.

The lesson was bigger than YouTube: Awareness does not have to be a blank check. TextNow could now evaluate upper-funnel channels against business outcomes and hold them to an efficiency standard.

![Image 7](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/63c00db03ecb8a822c829783/6a8c7d6f84398c398b6d2594_figure3_indexed_benchmark-outlined.svg)

**Figure 3.**Indexed cost per incremental Week 2 Primary User. YouTube finished just inside plan and below selected scaled prospecting tests. Lower is better. The comparison is directional because channel roles and test lengths differ.

> The incremental cost per registration was stronger than some of our direct-response campaigns. We also used the Week 2 Primary User trend to show the broader team how long it takes before we can expect to see lift from awareness media.

Gabriella Mark, Growth Marketing, TextNow

## Next steps

### A long test can answer a different question

The experiment did more than give TextNow a YouTube scorecard. It gave the company a timeline for interpreting future awareness campaigns.

When internal teams later saw installs increase during the first week of a larger brand launch, the growth team could point back to the experiment. TextNow launched YouTube in December, but the clearest Total W2PU gains emerged months later. An immediate lower-funnel impact was possible, but it was not the pattern this test had established.

> When teams asked whether a first-week increase in installs came from our new brand campaign, we could point to this test. We launched in December and saw the bulk of impact in March. That benchmark has been helpful for the internal team.

Nick Hughes, Growth Marketing Lead, TextNow

For TextNow, extending the test changed what the team could learn: not only whether lift appeared, but when the result became interpretable and how the measured outcome changed after treatment ended.

> Seeing results like this gives us confidence that this kind of media can work for us. It also helps us understand when to expect the impact, because the time horizon is very different.

Bonnie Herche, Vice President of Marketing, TextNow

TextNow entered the experiment asking whether YouTube could influence a lower-funnel business outcome. The complete read gave the organization a company-specific benchmark for when that impact became visible.

> I’m excited about the benchmarking this can provide as we make larger investments across the funnel. It gives us checkpoints and a measurement playbook for the campaigns to come.

Nick Hughes, Growth Marketing Lead, TextNow

The article frames brands across three levels: functional, experiential, and transformational, with the strongest brands shaping how customers see themselves. Emotional positioning builds stronger memory than repetition alone, so brands should identify the peak emotional experience they want customers to associate with the product and express it consistently. Brand leaders should then define a functional brand promise, translate its emotion into a slogan and cohesive visual system, and actively protect that system across every customer touchpoint. Title: How To Build an Inevitable Brand in 2026: A Guide To Modern Brand Strategy

URL Source: https://dribbble.com/stories/2026/08/25/cl-zlatina-petrova-brandly-modern-brand-strategy

Markdown Content:
_About the Author:_

_Zlatina Petrova has spent 13 years shaping brands and digital products across Silicon Valley and Europe. As Founder and Design Director of [Brandly](https://brandlycollective.com/), she works with tech startups, VCs, global brands and government institutions including work on Bulgaria’s national design system. Her work sits between branding, product design and UX/UI, with a belief that design should do more than look good: it should help businesses grow, products work better and brands mean something to people._

A few years ago, [Forbes](https://forbesbulgaria.com/2024/02/27/kak-brandly-promenya-igrata/) profiled Brandly. We started as a handful of home-based freelancer designers; now, we’re building B2B brand strategy at a national level for companies from Series A onward. The editor asked me whether I’d known Brandly would become what it is today. I said, **“**Yes. It was _inevitable_.” But it didn’t always feel that way.

An **inevitable brand**represents an idea whose time has come and spreads like wildfire. And the thing about inevitable brands is that they seem obvious in retrospect.

There was a time when we were just five people working from home, hunched over our computers. We were trying and trying to create Brandly. But at some point, after so many experiments, the brand took on a life of its own.

Just like great art, great brands come alive and begin to tell their creators how to bring them into existence. Michelangelo saw David in a five-meter block of marble. He didn’t create David; he set him free. David was already there.

**A great brand works the same way: it is discovered, revealed, and not simply created.**

But to discover it, we have to see past the beliefs and behaviors that get in the way. It’s a little like parenting: we don’t try to control our children and tell them exactly which career path to choose. We help them discover who they are.

Brands need the same space to reveal themselves.

Over the past seven years, building brands across industries and countries, we’ve learned that creating an inevitable brand often means stepping back before adding more.

Here are five ways to build an inevitable brand.

![Image 1](https://cdn.dribbble.com/uploads/71194/original/7597581a22ed88e0ea0f2fddb9da2fae.jpg?1787672819)
## **1. Uncover your corporate identity and brand truth**

Asking your customers who your brand should be is like asking strangers who you should become. Your brand’s truth doesn’t come from there. And it doesn’t come from an agency either. Going to an agency and asking them who you should be is like going to a therapist and asking them to present three different versions of the person you could become.

A good therapist guides you through the process of discovering the answer on your own. A [good branding partner](https://dribbble.com/hire/brand-designers) should do the same. Your brand’s truth and essence come from within: the founder’s vision, the reason the company exists, and the change it wants to create.

The job of corporate identity development is to uncover that truth, articulate it, and make it recognizable to your audience.

**Level 1: Functional brands**

This is where most brands live (and die). They compete on functional benefits, usually marginal differences such as “faster,” “cheaper,” “better,” or “a one-stop shop.” The problem is that there is so much competition at this level that brands experience constant downward pressure. If your primary advantage is being cheaper or faster, someone else can eventually become cheaper or faster than you.

**Level 2: Experiential brands**

Experiential brands still deliver functional benefits, but they add another layer: the experience of using the product or the service.

On a functional level, Ryanair sells you a plane ticket. It gets you from point A to point B. But have you ever been on a Ryanair flight? Let’s be honest, the experience isn’t the main reason you bought the ticket in the first place.

On the other hand, Virgin takes a different approach. You watch a movie, enjoy the service, and experience the personality of the brand throughout the journey. That is the difference between functional and experiential branding.

**Level 3: Transformational brands**

This is where iconic brands live. Transformational brands don’t just sell products or experiences. They create new human beings.

Before Nike, people jogged on the street. Nike helped make it aspirational to become a “weekend warrior.” This is someone who sees themselves as an athlete even if they aren’t a professional one.

Before Apple, if you showed up to work wearing a hoodie or a t-shirt you’d get fired. Apple created that generation of entrepreneurs, the disrupters.

**Pro tip: Discover which level your brand belongs to.**

We think about branding across three levels. Understanding which one fits your vision can help you see what kind of brand you are actually building.

![Image 2](https://cdn.dribbble.com/uploads/71195/original/4be647a8d76cde0984fd8bd0eba4f3e9.png?1787672896)
## **2. Build memory through emotional brand positioning, not just visual identity**

This is probably one of the most challenging ideas for founders. If you want to build an inevitable brand, you need to understand that becoming unforgettable starts with becoming memorable. And memory can be built in two ways: repetition and emotion.

Repetition is the traditional way of building memory. You repeat a message over and over until your audience starts repeating it too. The problem is that repetition is expensive.

A more powerful and most [cost-efficient way](https://dribbble.com/resources/tips/branding-agency-costs) of doing this is to create emotion. Emotion creates memory on a deeper level.

Memory attached to emotion is a survival mechanism. It’s the same reason you never forget the food that made you sick.

Brands can use the same principle: the extent to which you can consistently evoke that emotion is the extent to which your brand will be remembered.

**We call this brand frequency**, a crucial element of emotional brand positioning**.**

![Image 3](https://cdn.dribbble.com/uploads/71196/original/3084f3ee76887d87eb51984ca632afc4.jpg?1787672973)
**How do you discover your brand frequency?**

Start by identifying the peak experience of your brand, which is the emotional high point of the product experience.

![Image 4](https://cdn.dribbble.com/uploads/71197/original/44fa447d733ef894f1d5cb2b69bb57d7.jpg?1787673061)
When developing a B2B brand strategy for [Nexa](https://dribbble.com/shots/27647948-NEXA-AI-Robotics-Brand-Identity), a client of ours that is revolutionizing the workforce by introducing robots and AI agents into everyday business processes, the peak experience is the moment a founder opens their phone and sees that the work has been done without micromanaging anyone or even being at the office. The emotion is freedom and relief.

Now take an iconic brand like Airbnb. The peak experience is the moment you’re invited to sit at your host’s table, break bread, and share a meal. You may be in a foreign country, but somehow, you feel like you belong.

That is the art of branding: delivering the emotion before the customer even experiences the product.

**Takeaway:**The majority of communication between humans is non-verbal. That’s why what your brand emotes is more important than what your brand says to its audience.

## **3. Define your brand promise and positioning**

Another important step in building an inevitable brand is identifying your brand promise. It’s what you solve for your customer at a functional level better than anyone else.

This is what your brand _says_. Your brand frequency is what it _emotes_.

Brand promises are usually simple: “faster,” “simpler,” “cheaper,” and “easier.” But there is an important difference between a brand promise and a slogan.

**A brand promise describes what the brand does. A slogan emotes what the brand does.**

Think about slogans as pieces of poetry. They inspire, they emote, and they are the outcome of your brand’s frequency.

This is why blindly asking AI to give you 20 slogans becomes irrelevant. AI can be an excellent assistant in the brainstorming process. It can challenge directions, generate variations, organize thinking, and help you explore language faster.

But it should not be in charge of your decision as a brand leader. If the underlying emotion isn’t clear, generating another 100 slogans won’t reveal it. Human work comes first: discovering the truth. AI can then help you articulate it.

![Image 5](https://cdn.dribbble.com/uploads/71198/original/49707e8b72490608ece1b5af5db18730.jpg?1787673165)
For Nexa, the brand promise is to simplify business operations by solving workforce limitations.

The slogan we created for them is: **Beyond human scale.**

It carries the idea that technology isn’t separate from people. It is an extension of human capability that allows us to operate beyond our natural limitations. And the beautiful part about it? It also sounds great in other languages.

**Takeaway**: Brand promise is cognitive. Slogan is emotional.

![Image 6](https://cdn.dribbble.com/uploads/71199/original/22782bd791f6906b88667f65a8db6f49.jpg?1787673268)
## **4. Develop a cohesive visual identity system**

Once you understand the core elements of your brand universe, it’s time to translate them into a consistent visual identity system.

This is where many brands lose their way. They rediscover a new version of themselves with every presentation, campaign, landing page, social post, and product release.

But an inevitable brand should feel consistent everywhere. To help our clients find their way, we use a simple, yet effective technique called “the brand map.” The matrix helps us understand consumer perception by showing where a brand sits across two dimensions: price perception and identity. This becomes a blueprint for the brand’s visual language because design delivers emotion before a customer ever buys the product.

Once you know where your brand sits, decisions about typography, color, imagery, composition, and art direction become less subjective. Instead of asking, “Do we like this font?” you can ask, “Does this font communicate the perception we have chosen?”

The matrix has two axes: **Affordable-Expensive and Traditional-Modern**.

**Expensive + Traditional**

Serif typography, deep and muted color palettes, and moody photography that highlights craftsmanship, heritage, and texture.

**Expensive + Modern**

An ultra-minimalist, futuristic aesthetic. A lot of white space, clean geometric sans-serif fonts, highly restricted color palettes, often monochromatic with sharp metallic accents and abstract or conceptual imagery.

**Affordable + Traditional**

A familiar, warm, and inviting visual language. Friendly fonts, approachable earthy or primary tones, and authentic, human-centric photography focused on everyday people and real-life moments.

**Affordable + Modern**

A high-energy, vibrant, digital-first visual language. Bold layouts, bright color accents, high contrast, clean neo-grotesque typography, and dynamic imagery designed for a screen-first generation.

## **5. How to hire a branding agency and direct your team**

You know the saying: “If you want something done right, do it yourself.”

Brand building is one of the places where we would challenge that idea.

You shouldn’t design every asset yourself. But you also shouldn’t completely outsource the responsibility for your brand either. You need to play many roles and take each of them seriously.

**Hire**

When looking to [hire a branding agency](https://dribbble.com/branding-agency) or freelance designer, look for a branding partner who is great at creating a mood. They understand how visual decisions affect the nervous system of the viewer and can translate your emotional brand positioning into typography, color, imagery, composition, and movement.

One way to test this when evaluating outsourced brand design is to ask the designer to create a mood board based on your brand emotion. Then show it to several people. Don’t ask them, “Do you like it?” Ask them: “How does this make you feel?” If the mood board consistently evokes your brand emotion, you may have found the right design partner.

**Direct**

Once you find the right partner, your second role as a brand leader is to direct.

Ask the designer to deconstruct, distill, complement, and document each part of the visual system:

*   Colors
*   Typography
*   Logo
*   Iconography
*   Photography
*   Motion
*   Layout principles

These elements form the foundation of your style guide. We also strongly recommend adding real brand applications and mockups across every customer touchpoint: website, social media, video, graphic design, UX, UI, presentations, sales materials, and anything else your team uses regularly.

Identify which assets are most critical and build those first.

**Evangelize**

The final role is often forgotten. A style guide sitting in a folder doesn’t create consistency. People do. Once the system exists, someone has to protect it, explain it, teach it, and make sure the team understands not only _what_ the rules are, but _why_ they exist.

That is what turns a visual identity into a living brand. And it brings us back to where we started. An inevitable brand is not something you manufacture in Figma. You discover its truth. You identify the emotion behind it. You articulate its promise. You translate it into a recognizable system. And then you protect that system without suffocating it.

The goal of any successful B2B brand strategy isn’t to control every expression of the brand. It is to understand the brand deeply enough to let it reveal itself. And eventually, the right decisions start to feel obvious. Almost inevitable.

Title: Reddit is the keyword research tool you’re probably not using

URL Source: https://searchengineland.com/reddit-keyword-research-tool-485859

Published Time: 2026-08-27T14:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
Almost every conversation about [Reddit](https://searchengineland.com/reddit-seo-453406) and [SEO](https://searchengineland.com/guide/what-is-seo) in the last two years has focused on participation. Should you post? Comment? Pay someone to seed a thread? Build a subreddit?

Those are the wrong questions.

Reddit is a massive repository of ranking data that can reveal what your audience is searching for and where your content falls short.

It ranks for hundreds of millions of keywords, with millions ranking on Page 1. It also surfaces in millions of [AI Overview](https://searchengineland.com/guide/google-ai-overviews) queries. That data is publicly visible in a tool you’re probably already paying for.

You don’t need a Reddit account. You need a Semrush login and about two hours.

I saw this firsthand with an enterprise travel client. Reddit eventually became one of its top three competitors by Organic Share of Voice. A threat analysis uncovered opportunities for net-new content, existing content optimization, and an FAQ library. The client wasn’t even aware of the branded Reddit community around its brand.

The process turns Reddit’s organic footprint into a content roadmap: the questions your audience is asking, the ones your site doesn’t answer, and the ones AI systems are already citing Reddit for.

## Why Reddit is worth mining

As of August, Semrush data shows reddit.com ranking for roughly 166 million keywords, including more than 10 million in position No. 1, 31 million in the top three, and 65 million on page one. More than 35 million of those keywords trigger AI Overviews, with Reddit cited in more than 15 million – a 46% citation rate.

Two developments helped drive this:

*   **Google partnership:** Signed in February 2024, the same day Reddit filed for its IPO, and reportedly worth about [$60 million a year](https://searchengineland.com/reddit-google-ai-content-licensing-deal-437782). The deal gave Google real-time access to Reddit content through its Data API. Reddit’s SERP visibility had already started climbing in late 2023, but the partnership accelerated it. Google’s “hidden gems” and “helpful content” updates were rewarding Reddit even before the agreement.
*   **OpenAI partnership:** Announced three months later and estimated at around $70 million annually, it gave ChatGPT a pipeline into fresher, more conversational content.

The result is a platform that functions as a de facto source of information for both traditional search and generative answers. It’s driven Reddit to become one of the most visited websites on the planet. Its August estimated traffic is now up to 440 million monthly organic visits, according to Semrush.

There’s a wrinkle worth knowing about. In July, [The Wall Street Journal reported](https://www.wsj.com/business/media/google-search-publishers-ai-content-0fb06e41) that Reddit was weighing whether to renew its agreement with Google — even considering restricting Google’s structured AI access — because AI Overviews have eroded referral traffic across the web. Reddit’s stock dropped roughly 9% on the news.

The negotiation is ongoing. Reddit’s dominance in the SERP depends in part on business arrangements that can change. That makes the data worth mining now.

**_Dig deeper: [A smarter Reddit strategy for organic and AI search visibility](https://searchengineland.com/a-smarter-reddit-strategy-for-organic-and-ai-search-visibility-459369)_**

[Be the brand customers find first. Track, grow, and measure your visibility across Google, AI search, social, local, and every channel that influences buying decisions. Start your free trial](https://www.semrush.com/?utm_campaign=ic_sel_0101default&utm_source=searchengineland.com&utm_medium=overlay&onboarding=off)
## Reddit as a query layer

When Reddit outranks you for “best running shoes for flat feet,” that ranking is telling you something specific: A real person asked that question in language a real person uses, other real people answered it, and Google decided that exchange was the best available result.

Reddit didn’t win because of technical SEO. It won because it had the answer in a format people trusted. You can’t replicate the format. You can absolutely answer the question.

That’s the whole exercise. Reddit’s ranking footprint is a map of unmet informational demand in your category, already sorted by what Google has decided is worth surfacing.

Before you start, establish whether Reddit is actually a competitive factor in your vertical. Spend 30 minutes running the Domain Overview filter on two or three of your core non-brand themes or terms and look at the raw count. That number tells you most of what you need to know.

Niche B2B, regulated, highly technical, or specific/narrow categories: Reddit’s influence is often muted or more limited. The conversations exist, but they’re small, and Google isn’t ranking them. In those verticals, this analysis will produce a thin list, and you should spend your time elsewhere — but it’s worth doing the analysis first to discover that.

Larger consumer brands, competitive retail, health, finance, software, travel, and anything with an opinionated buying process: Reddit is almost certainly outranking you on hundreds, if not thousands, of queries, and the gap analysis will produce more work than you can staff.

Knowing which one you’re in before you build the deck saves you from presenting a threat that isn’t there.

**_Dig deeper: [Reddit’s AI search influence goes beyond training data](https://searchengineland.com/reddits-ai-search-influence-goes-beyond-training-data-478235)_**

## How to mine Reddit’s rankings for content opportunities

You’ll need Semrush. Two reports do most of the work: Domain Overview and Keyword Gap.

### Step 1: Pull Reddit’s non-brand rankings in your category

Open Domain Overview, enter reddit.com, and go to the Organic Research report.

Under Advanced Filters, set _Include → Keyword → Containing_, then enter a non-brand term tied to your products or services. Since I’m an avid runner and did this same analysis for a running shoe company, for this example, let’s use “running” as the main category. Use one core theme at a time, like “running shoe” or “women’s running shoe.”

Apply a _Position_ filter set to _Top 10_, hit apply, and export to Excel.

You now have every query in that theme where Reddit holds a top-10 position. If the theme is broad and the list is really long, tighten to Top 3 positions. If it’s thin, loosen it. The right cutoff depends entirely on how much volume the topic has.

Repeat for your three to five core non-brand themes. Don’t do more than that on a first pass — you’ll drown in rows before you’ve built any judgment about what matters.

Depending on the industry and niche, this will help identify how much of a threat Reddit is to your brand and industry. Sometimes when I’ve run this analysis, I don’t find anything worthwhile. Other times, I can find tens of thousands of keywords.

![Image 1: Image 144](blob:http://localhost/e9d47e1eb47e106f7c01a6a5bfc26fb8)

### Step 2: Isolate the AI Overview layer

This is the step most people skip, and it’s the one that pays off in 2026. Reddit consistently shows up in AI-powered search as a cited source.

Stay in the same report. Remove the position filter. Open the _SERP Features_ filter, go to _SERP Features on SERP_, and select _AI Overviews._

Export that list to Excel.

What you’re looking at is every query in your theme where Reddit appears on a SERP that also generates an AI Overview. Reddit is cited in more than 15 million of those queries.

Feed this export directly into your prompt research. These queries are the raw material for the questions you should be testing in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity to see whether your brand shows up at all.

**Bonus:** If you use the custom RegEx to identify potential prompts in the domain’s Google Search Console data, you can marry these two data sets using your favorite LLM. I used Claude.

![Image 2: Image 147](blob:http://localhost/c9a72b5d0cfe0d1774a7c8e36a50b278)

**_Dig deeper: [How to build an organic Reddit strategy that drives SEO impact](https://searchengineland.com/build-organic-reddit-strategy-seo-impact-464698)_**

Get the newsletter search marketers rely on.

* * *

### Step 3: Run the branded pass

Now filter for your own brand name and your competitors’ brand names. What comes back is usually one of two things, and both are useful.

*   **Bottom-of-funnel support content:** People asking whether your product is worth it, why a feature broke, how to cancel, or whether a workaround exists. This is a customer support FAQ written by your customers. If Reddit is ranking for “does [your product] work with [integration]” and your own help center isn’t, that’s not a Reddit problem.
*   **Comparison content further up the funnel:**Examples include “[your brand] vs. [competitor],” “[competitor] alternatives,” or “is [your brand] better than [competitor].” These are high-intent queries where a thread of strangers is currently shaping the narrative about your product.

You can’t remove those threads. You can publish something better and get cited alongside them.

Additionally, I would run the branded analysis on three to five of your closest organic competitors.

![Image 3: Image 145](blob:http://localhost/a335375889b1947f0993fe6324435294)

### Step 4: Run the Keyword Gap report

Open the Keyword Gap report. Put your domain in the first field, add reddit.com as a competitor, and keep both set to Root Domain and Organic Keywords. Compare.

Click the _Weak_ tab, set the position filter for competitors to _Top 10_, apply, and export. Note — you might need to limit it to Top 3 depending on the industry, domain, and volume of keywords. You can also filter by search volume and sort by queries with 100 or 250 average monthly searches or more.

You now have every keyword where you and Reddit both rank, and Reddit ranks better — filtered to positions that actually get impressions.

The Weak tab matters more than the Missing tab. Missing keywords are speculative. You have no proof you can compete, and most aren’t related specifically to your brand, industry, or product. Weak keywords mean Google already considers your page relevant enough to rank. You’re not building from zero. You’re closing a gap on pages that already have a foothold.

![Image 4: Image 146](blob:http://localhost/b18e3ea097642334db711cdae6618f21)

**_Dig deeper: [10 Reddit comment frameworks that drive engagement without sounding like ads](https://searchengineland.com/reddit-comment-frameworks-471044)_**

## What to do with the exports

Four files, one job: turn them into a topical map. Cluster the non-brand exports by theme and intent, then compare that map against your existing content.

You’ll typically find three buckets:

*   **Optimization candidates:** You have a page, it ranks, and Reddit ranks better. Usually, the fix is depth and specificity — Reddit wins on the long tail of qualifiers your page glosses over.
*   **Net-new creation:** Reddit ranks, and you have nothing. Prioritize by cluster density, not individual volume. Twenty related questions with modest volume each is a stronger content brief than one head term.
*   **FAQ and support content:**Mostly from the branded pass. It’s fast to produce, disproportionately effective for AI citation, and it takes a conversation currently happening on someone else’s platform and gives it a home on yours.

One tracking note: Add reddit.com as a tracked competitor in Semrush Position Tracking, and — if you’re running prompt-level visibility monitoring in a tool like Peec AI — add it there, too.

## What this isn’t

This isn’t a Reddit activation strategy. Nothing in this process involves posting, commenting, seeding, or otherwise participating on the platform. That’s a separate discipline with real risk — Reddit communities are unusually good at detecting and punishing brand astroturfing, and the downside of getting caught outweighs the upside of a well-placed comment.

The exercise here is pure keyword intelligence. You’re using one of the largest ranking datasets in your category to improve your own topical authority on your own domain.

**Bonus tip:**One valuable Reddit takeaway for your PR and social teams is which Reddit communities and subreddit threads are ranking for your industry and brand.

[Own the conversation before your competitors. See where your brand appears, where it doesn’t, and exactly how to win more visibility across search, AI, local, social, and every channel that matters. Start your free trial](https://www.semrush.com/?utm_campaign=ic_sel_0102default&utm_source=searchengineland.com&utm_medium=overlay&onboarding=off)
## Turn Reddit’s ranking footprint into a content roadmap

Reddit spent two decades accumulating the exact thing search engines and language models now want most: real people answering real questions in real language.

You can’t buy that. But you can read the map it produced, find the questions your category is asking, and answer them better on a property you actually control.

Start with the threat assessment. Then run the gap. What content do you need to add? What content do you need to optimize?

kept.heading: SHALLOW INTENT: WHY PEOPLE DON'T LIKE AI CONTENT, AND HOW TO MAKE IT GREAT (16 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI content decouples two things that used to move together: how polished something looks and how much thought went into it. Models recombine statistical patterns from everything they've seen rather than reasoning through each choice, so the result can look intricate while containing contradictions a human creator would never make, mismatched historical details, textures that ghost and repeat.
